data.title: Time for a Grand Bargain on Debt — Barrons.com
data.description:
To the Editor: Jack Hough's debt analysis is admirably honest, but it understates the real constraint: The dollar's reserve status buys time, not political will — and time is the one resource being spent fastest ("The New Congress Must Fix the $40 Trillion Debt — and Soon," Cover Story, Nov. 5). The U.S. can borrow cheaply because global capital values American growth and liquidity, not fiscal virtue. But that advantage isn't unconditional. The danger isn't a sudden bond-vigilante strike; it's a gradual repricing of the haven premium as investors see the threshold for political action rising while the capacity for it falls.

The arithmetic sets the deadline. Political will determines whether we meet it. A grand bargain addressing entitlements, revenue, and spending is the surest way to preserve the buffer we're currently consuming. Inflation, growth, or muddling through cannot substitute for the political choices that will otherwise fall to the next generation that Hough invokes.

Brian J. Gross Austin, Texas

Don't Freak Out

To the Editor: This may be a moment for caution rather than panic ("Everything Is Going Wrong for Chip Stocks. 5 Names at Fire-Sale Prices," Nov. 5). When markets move sharply, it's worth stepping back and recalibrating, but not rushing to the exits.

Data-center projects are already under way around the world. Many have received approvals, and some have everything on order including turbines, etc. Remember, it takes months to build a complete compute warehouse.

Russ Erickson On Barrons.com

Data-Center Plug

To the Editor: As a decades-long Amazon.com shareholder — I bought my first shares in 1999) — a positive article on the company is welcome and, unfortunately, uncommon in the Wall Street press ("Why Amazon and Other AI Data-Center Stocks Will Be Post-Midterm Winners," Tech Trader, Nov. 6).

I must wonder how anyone who has thought about it feels that data centers are bad for the community, state, or country. I understand you don't want a copper smelter or uranium mine in your county, but a data center? That's unbelievable.

Doug Thompson On Barrons.com

Betting on Summit

To the Editor: Great article, thanks ("The U.S. Stocks Quietly Winning the Chinese Drug Boom," Nov. 3). I'll check out Summit Therapeutics and others. It looks like they are conducting trials across U.S. to comply with the Food and Drug Administration. Hopefully, the increased competition will bring down prices for us consumers.

Ashish Deshpande On Barrons.com

data.description:
CALGARY, Alberta, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NEX: CWV.H: Crown Point Energy Inc. (“Crown Point”, the “Company”, "our" or "we") today announced its financial and operating results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. All dollar figures are expressed in United States dollars ("USD") unless otherwise stated.

In the following discussion, the three months ended September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026 may be referred to as “Q3 2026” and “Q2 2026”, respectively. The comparative three months ended September 30, 2025, may be referred to as “Q3 2025”.

Q3 2026 SUMMARY

During Q3 2026, the Company:

  • Reported net cash used in operating activities and funds flow provided by operating activities of $8.2 million and $9.7 million, respectively, as compared to Q3 2025 when the Company reported net cash and funds flow used in operating activities of $3.6 million and $3.5 million, respectively; 
  • Earned $51.8 million of oil and natural gas sales revenue on total average daily sales volumes of 6,933 BOE per day1, higher than $21.7 million of oil and natural gas sales revenue on total average daily sales volumes of 4,182 BOE per day2 in Q3 2025 due to oil sales from the Chubut concessions acquired in the fourth quarter of 2025. The Company’s average daily sales volumes in Q3 2026 were lower than the 9,158 BOE per day reported in Q2 2026 due to a delayed oil shipment from the Chubut concessions, which resulted in higher oil inventory at September 30, 2026;
  • Average daily production volumes for Q3 2026 were 8,042 BOE per day, lower than 8,531 BOE per day in Q2 2026 mainly due to the expiration of the Tierra del Fuego (“TDF”) concessions on August 18, 2026 and higher than 4,348 BOE per day in Q3 2025 mainly due to oil production volumes from the Chubut concessions.
  • Received an average of $5.87 per mcf for natural gas and $86.60 per bbl for crude oil compared to $3.84 per mcf for natural gas and $62.83 per bbl for oil received in Q3 2025;
  • Reported an operating netback of $20.95 per BOE3 up from $(6.60) per BOE in Q3 2025;
  • Issued $16.5 million of discounted promissory notes and repaid $21.1 million of working capital loans and discounted promissory notes;
  • Completed a rights offering for gross proceeds of $30 million, the proceeds of which were used to repay the $29.9 million loan from Liminar Energía S.A. (“Liminar”), the Company’s largest shareholder;
  • Issued $8.26 million principal amount of Series X Notes and $46.77 million principal amount of Series XI Notes, of which $25.0 million was issued in exchange for the surrender and cancellation of the $25 million principal amount of Series VII Notes;
  • Recognized a $1.1 million loss on the expiration of the TDF concessions on August 18, 2026;
  • Effective September 11, 2026, transferred its listing to the NEX Board of the TSX Venture Exchange, with its trading symbol changing to “CWV.H”;
  • Reported income before taxes of $0.1 million, deferred tax provision of $2.7 million and net loss of $2.6 million, as compared to Q3 2025 when the Company reported loss before taxes of $8.7 million, deferred tax recovery of $3.9 million and net loss of $4.8 million; and
  • Reported a working capital deficit4 of $51.7 million at September 30, 2026, as compared to a working capital deficit of $71.8 million at December 31, 2025.

SUBSEQUENT EVENTS

On October 30, 2026, the Company repaid the first principal installment of the Series VI Notes in the amount of $7.3 million, and the Company paid the first principal installment of the Series IX Notes in the amount of $3 million.

OPERATIONAL UPDATE

Chubut Concessions

  • During Q3 2026, El Tordillo concession oil production averaged 4,182 (net 3,973) bbls of oil per day, La Tapera concession oil production averaged 28 (net 27) bbls of oil per day and Puesto Quiroga concession oil production averaged 160 (net 152) bbls of oil per day. Natural gas production from the El Tordillo and Puesto Quiroga concessions averaged 2,422 (net 2,301) mcf per day. During Q3 2026, the Company drilled the PQO-2005 well to a total depth of 3,618 metres and performed workovers on 12 oil producing wells in the El Tordillo concession perforating new zones in the Comodoro Rivadavia and Mina del Carmen formations.

Santa Cruz Concessions

  • During Q3 2026, Piedra Clavada concession oil production averaged 1,683 bbls of oil per day and Koluel Kaike concession oil production averaged 944 bbls of oil per day. During Q3 2026, the Company completed workovers on two oil producing wells in the Piedra Clavada concession and completed several interventions on oil wells in both the Koluel Kaike and Piedra Clavada concessions.

Mendoza Concessions

  • Oil production for Q3 2026 averaged 836 (net 418) bbls of oil per day from the Chañares Herrados concession and 162 (net 81) bbls of oil per day from the Puesto Pozo Cercado Oriental concession.

TDF Concessions

  • During Q3 2026, San Martin oil production averaged 220 (net 106) bbls of oil per day; Las Violetas concession natural gas production averaged 6,923 (net 3,346) mcf per day and associated oil production averaged 25 (net 12) bbls of oil per day.The TDF concessions, in which the Company held a 48.3275% non-operating participating interest, expired on August 18, 2026. The averages reported are for the period from July 1 to August 18, 2026.

OUTLOOK

  • The Company’s capital spending for fiscal 2026 is budgeted at approximately $44.8 million, of which: $32.2 million is allocated to the Chubut concessions for well workovers, facilities improvements and a drilling campaign comprised of 4 wells; $11.3 million is allocated to the Santa Cruz concessions for well workovers, facilities improvements and a drilling campaign comprised of 3 wells; and $1.3 million is allocated to the Mendoza concessions for well workovers and facilities improvements. data.title: SpaceX Flight 15 booster diverts to splashdown, missing planned double catch
data.description:
SpaceX’s Super Heavy booster diverted to an ocean splashdown instead of returning for capture by the launch tower’s mechanical arms during Starship Flight 15, according to the live mission update provided for this report. The reason for the aborted capture wasn't immediately clear.

The diversion ends the mission’s prospect of achieving SpaceX’s planned first recovery of both rocket stages using tower catches. The company had intended to catch Super Heavy shortly after launch, followed by the Starship upper stage after a much longer orbital mission. The catches were planned as separate events, roughly a day apart.

The Starship upper stage continued toward its planned orbit, according to the same live update. Its mission objectives include deploying 26 next-generation Starlink V3 internet satellites and attempting its first return to the launch site for a tower catch. Orbital insertion, satellite deployment and upper-stage recovery remained unconfirmed at the stage described here. Space.com

For investors, the booster diversion leaves a key part of SpaceX’s intended operating model undemonstrated on this flight: recovering both stages for reuse. Routine recovery and repeated flights would help establish whether Starship can deliver the lower launch costs and higher flight frequency underpinning its commercial ambitions.

Satellite deployment remains a separate milestone. Completing that objective would advance Starship’s role in expanding SpaceX’s Starlink network, even with the booster catch abandoned.

In July, SunPower said Q2 results were hurt by issues at SunPower Direct and that management changes were expected to help Q3 results.

SunPower said it expects to file its 10-Q within the five-day grace period.

data.title: Coffee Stain enters into agreement to acquire Chronicles: Medieval IP
data.description:
Coffee Stain Group AB (publ) (“Coffee Stain”) has entered into an agreement to acquire the intellectual property rights and related assets to the game Chronicles: Medieval from the bankruptcy estate of Raw Power Games. The purchase price amounts to DKK 36.75 million in cash and the assets will be acquired by a newly established company, owned 75 per cent by Coffee Stain and 25 per cent by a small group of key members of the game’s original development team.

Raw Power Games, the Copenhagen-based studio behind Chronicles: Medieval, was declared bankrupt on 30 October 2026. The bankruptcy estate subsequently carried out a sale process for the studio’s assets, in which Coffee Stain submitted the winning bid.

“Chronicles: Medieval made a strong impression at its reveal at Summer Game Fest last year. We’re happy to step in and help bring it to the players after the recent developments in Copenhagen. Chronicles: Medieval ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group. Things have been moving fast around this deal, and our short-term focus will be on working out how best to complete the game, together with the new company’s management team,” says Anton Westbergh, CEO of Coffee Stain.

Chronicles: Medieval is a medieval sandbox game in which players build and command armies, fight alongside their troops in large-scale battles and shape their own journey. It has been in development since 2022 and ranks among the top 30 most wishlisted games on Steam as of today. The game’s Steam page currently states a release window of 2027. Further information about the plans for the game, including the release timeline, will be communicated through the game’s own channels in due course.

Transaction and financial impact

Coffee Stain has entered into an investment agreement with the new company, under which Coffee Stain will hold 75 per cent of the shares and fund the full purchase price for the assets, as well as the continued development of the game.

The new company subsequently entered into an asset purchase agreement with the bankruptcy estate, under which it acquires the intellectual property rights to the game and all related assets. The purchase price amounts to DKK 36.75 million in cash, excluding transaction costs.

The new company starts with a limited cost base, which is expected to increase gradually as the studio takes shape. Coffee Stain Group will report on the financial impact in its interim reports.

Completion of the transaction

The transaction will be completed when the purchase price is paid to the bankruptcy estate, which is expected in the coming weeks. Completion is not subject to any other conditions.

Advisors

Plesner Advokatpartnerselskab acted as legal M&A and strategic advisor. Rosengrens law firm (Sweden) and Moalem Weitemeyer (Denmark) acted as legal counsel to Coffee Stain Group in the transaction.

data.title: JPMorgan's Top Credit Cards Executive Is Leaving the Bank — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Rebecca Ungarino

The executive responsible for JPMorgan Chase's vast credit card business, among the largest in the world, is leaving the bank, according to an internal memo viewed by Barron's.

Allison Beer, the CEO of card and connected commerce, "has informed me of her decision to leave the firm for an external opportunity," JPMorgan Co-President Troy Rohrbaugh said in a memo on Friday.

"She and her team have played an important part in moving our card business to where it is today," he said in the memo to employees.

Beer's exit is notable because she is among the most powerful leaders in the credit card industry. JPMorgan's card business is among the world's largest by customer spending and balances. She is leaving for another company at a moment when banks are fiercely competing to win over cardholders, especially those who are higher earners.

Rohrbaugh's team plans to name a new leader for the card and connected commerce businesses in the coming weeks, he wrote. In the meantime, those who reported to Beer will report to Rohrbaugh, who is the CEO of consumer and community banking.

A JPMorgan spokesman declined to specify who will replace Beer. Beer didn't immediately respond to Barron's request for comment.

Beer joined JPMorgan in 2017 as a top payments executive from American Express.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

data.title: First Horizon Bank, Catholic Charities and AltCap Leverage New Markets Tax Credits to Build $25 Million Family Opportunity Center
data.description:
HOUSTON, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- First Horizon Bank () (or "First Horizon") today announced it is working alongside Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston and AltCap to implement an innovative financing solution to build a new 60,000-square-foot facility that will significantly improve access to food and other services for low-income Houstonians. The new Family Opportunity Center in north Houston will leverage New Markets Tax Credits (NMTC) provided by First Horizon Bank and the Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) AltCap.

Slated to open its doors in 2028, the Family Opportunity Center will feature a market-style food pantry, thrift store, and access to the nonprofit's services, including mental health counseling, parenting classes, rental assistance and job readiness resources. It will also provide space for community and first responders during natural disasters, along with ample warehouse space for food storage.

The total investment for the center, located at 9111 Jensen Drive, is $25 million. To date, Catholic Charities has raised $17.5 million in private and foundation gifts. The NMTC represents nearly 10 percent of the total needed.

Congress established the NMTC to encourage private-sector investment in low-income communities, including the future location of the Family Opportunity Center. Under the program, CDFIs such as AltCap are awarded tax credit allocations from the U.S. Department of the Treasury and deploy them to support projects that deliver measurable community benefits. Investors, including financial institutions like First Horizon Bank, receive federal tax credits in exchange for qualified investments. This investment structure enables community-serving projects, such as the Family Opportunity Center, to access favorable financing and move forward when traditional financing alone may be insufficient.

"We are proud to work alongside Catholic Charities and AltCap to provide financing for the Family Opportunity Center," said Yasmin Huebinger, Houston Commercial Banking Leader for First Horizon Bank. "This investment reflects First Horizon's commitment to strengthening the communities we serve, expanding economic opportunities and driving sustainable growth that benefits families and the broader Houston community."

"As Catholic Charities continues its Building to Serve Capital Campaign, the Family Opportunity Center stands as a testament to what can be achieved when nonprofit organizations, community development partners and financial institutions align resources around a shared vision," said Michael D. Hansen, president and CEO of Catholic Charities. "The cooperation among Catholic Charities, AltCap and First Horizon Bank illustrates how innovative financing can help transform lives and strengthen communities across the Houston region."

"As a CDFI that has been helping to increase access to capital for Houston entrepreneurs and small businesses since 2022, AltCap is excited to demonstrate how we can also support high impact community investments like the Family Opportunity Center using the NMTC Program," said Ruben Alonso III, CEO of AltCap. "We look forward to continuing to bring capital and other resources to underserved communities and small businesses throughout Houston as well as Harris County."

The Catholic Charities Family Opportunity Center is AltCap's first NMTC investment in Texas. Since its founding, AltCap has deployed nearly $350 million in capital, from microloans to NMTC financing, to entrepreneurs and communities often overlooked and underserved by traditional financial institutions.

For more information about Catholic Charities' Family Opportunity Center, visit the Catholic Charities website.

Through a network of life-changing programs that work together to alleviate poverty, we serve thousands of people each year from locations in Harris, Fort Bend and Galveston counties. As the social services arm of the Archdiocese, we are guided by the Catholic faith to serve people of all beliefs in achieving self-sufficiency so they can live with dignity. data.title: Organigram Provides NASDAQ Listing Update
data.description:
Organigram Global Inc. () () (the “Company” or “Organigram”), Canada's #1 cannabis company by market share¹ and a growing global cannabis platform, today announced that on November 11, 2026, it received notification (the “Notification”) from The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) that it is not in compliance with the minimum bid price requirement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) for continued listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The Notification was issued because the closing bid price of the Company's common shares was below US$1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days. Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) requires listed common shares to maintain a minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share (the “Minimum Bid Requirement”), while Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a deficiency exists when the requirement is not met for 30 consecutive business days.

The Notification has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company's common shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. Pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), the Company has 180 calendar days, until May 10, 2027, to regain compliance with the Minimum Bid Requirement. To regain compliance, the closing bid price of the Company's common shares must be at least US$1.00 per share for a minimum of 10 consecutive business days during the compliance period, subject to Nasdaq's discretion to extend this period.

If the Company does not regain compliance by May 10, 2027, it may be eligible for an additional 180-calendar-day compliance period, subject to satisfying applicable Nasdaq requirements, including transferring its listing to the Nasdaq Capital Market. If the Company does not qualify for an additional compliance period, its common shares may become subject to delisting proceedings, subject to applicable appeal rights.

The Company's common shares are also listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, and the Notification does not affect the Company's listing or compliance status on that exchange.

About Organigram

Organigram Global Inc. is listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market and TSX. The Company's wholly owned subsidiary, Organigram Inc., is a licensed cultivator and processor. Through its acquisition of Sanity Group GmbH ("Sanity Group"), Organigram participates in the German medical cannabis market and other emerging markets within Europe. Organigram is focused on producing high-quality cannabis for adult consumers, as well as extending the Company's global footprint. Organigram has also developed and acquired a portfolio of cannabis brands, including Edison, Big Bag O' Buds, SHRED, Monjour, Tremblant, Collective Project, Trailblazer, BOXHOT and DEBUNK. Through its acquisition of Sanity Group, Organigram's European brands include Vayamed, avaay, ZOIKS, Endosane Pharmaceuticals, VAAY, and Grashaus Projects. Organigram operates facilities in Moncton, New Brunswick and Lac Supérieur, Quebec, with a dedicated edibles manufacturing facility in Winnipeg, Manitoba. The Company also operates two additional cannabis processing facilities in Southwestern Ontario; one in Aylmer and the other in London. The facility in Aylmer houses best-in-class extraction capabilities, and is optimized for formulation refinement, post-processing of minor cannabinoids, and infused pre-roll production. The facility in London will be optimized for labelling, packaging, and national fulfillment. The Company is regulated by Health Canada under the Cannabis Act and the Cannabis Regulations.

data.title: More Than 10,000 Flights Delayed or Canceled in FAA's Nationwide Groundstop — WSJ
data.description:
By Andrew Tangel, Jacob Passy and Alison Sider

The Federal Aviation Administration halted departing flights nationwide Friday afternoon, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns after air-traffic control communications were disrupted.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wrote on X that there had been a communication issue affecting multiple air route traffic-control centers, which handle high-altitude flights covering large swaths of the country. "FAA technicians are investigating the issue," he wrote.

Planes in the air are able to continue flying to their destinations, an FAA spokeswoman said. Inbound international flights will be managed on a case-by-case basis, the agency said.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House on Friday that "there was no prior indication, or indication as of yet, that this was a nefarious attack against us. This is a telecommunications outage as of now." When asked if it could be a cyberattack, Mullin said officials weren't ruling anything out yet.

"There's no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones," Mullin said, adding this isn't "another 9/11."

The groundstop started Friday afternoon at 3:53 p.m. ET. More than 1,100 U.S. flights had been canceled and nearly 10,000 had been delayed as of Friday at 5:40 p.m. ET, according to FlightAware. As of around 4 p.m., there were still roughly 11,000 flights scheduled to depart from U.S. airports Friday, according to aviation analytics company Cirium.

On social media, travelers reported that taxiing planes were turned around at airports to return to gates and passengers were being deplaned, with flight crews signaling the delays could last hours. Others said they were stuck on aircraft as gates filled with passengers.

At Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, word quickly spread among travelers while ground traffic appeared to suddenly stop on the tarmac late Friday afternoon. By early evening, telecom issues at some FAA air-traffic facilities were coming back online, according to people familiar with the matter.

The outage appears to be affecting a telecommunications network overseen by L3Harris Technologies, according to people briefed on the matter. The network handles crucial radio frequencies that air-traffic controllers use to communicate with pilots, the people said. It wasn't immediately clear whether the outage also affected the radar feeds that controllers use to keep aircraft safely separated in the skies.

An L3Harris spokeswoman didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

United Airlines said it is responding to the ground stop and will work with customers to get them to destinations once the issue is resolved. American said it expects its schedule to be disrupted for the rest of the day, depending how long the groundstop remains in place.

"It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop," American said in a statement.

More than 440 U.S. flights had been canceled and 9,000 had been delayed as of Friday at 5 p.m. ET, according to FlightAware.

John Sturino, a musician who plays the drums, said he is going to miss a percussion convention in Indianapolis because of the flight delay. The Brooklyn native said he had been waiting half an hour in line to cancel his flight at the Delta lounge desk in LaGuardia Airport and get a refund.

"It wasn't worth staying in the airport," he said.

Wedding photographer Christian Shackton was also waiting at LaGuardia Airport for a Southwest flight to Dallas for a work event. He considered himself lucky that he had already grabbed a spot at one of the terminal's restaurants before the flight delays began rolling in.

"The airport is a fun experience right now," he said. "If you're in a seat, stay in that seat or you will be fighting for a spot to relax while this gets sorted."

He said he had not yet received any notifications by email or through the Southwest app regarding the situation.

This is the second time in recent years the FAA has taken the extraordinary step of halting all departures across the country.

In 2023, a nationwide ground stop was ordered amid an outage of the FAA's Notice to Airmen system, which provides critical information to pilots. That order lasted for two hours, contributing to more than 1,000 flight cancellations. Before that, the FAA had only taken that step on Sept. 11, 2001.

The nation's air-traffic control system has been beset by communications issues leading to radio and radar outages that have affected various FAA facilities in recent years. Earlier this year, flights at New York-area airports were halted when a contractor accidentally cut a fiber communications line in New Jersey.

Other outages that have affected the Dallas area, Upper Midwest and New York City area have been relatively contained.

It wasn't immediately clear whether the telecommunications outages affected both radios controllers use to communicate with pilots, or also radar that they need to keep planes safely separated.

Updates to follow as news develops.
